name: Z(π) commutes through W
summary: A Pauli Z on the input of a W-spider can be pushed onto all of its outputs.
description:
The W-spider (black triangle) with one input and $n$ outputs maps $|0\rangle \mapsto |0\cdots 0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle \mapsto |10\cdots0\rangle + |010\cdots0\rangle + \cdots + |0\cdots01\rangle$: it spreads a single excitation over its outputs in all possible ways. The small dot marks its input leg.

Every term in the image of $|1\rangle$ has exactly one output in state $|1\rangle$, so a sign $-1$ on the input is the same as a sign $-1$ on every output. In Hadzihasanovic's ZW-calculus, where the binary white vertex is the Pauli Z, this says that the binary white vertex is an automorphism of the black monoid (axiom 3b, generalised to $n$ outputs as $\mathrm{am}_W^n$).

The same argument works for any diagonal map $\mathrm{diag}(1,r)$: see [weights copy through W](../w-weight-copy/).
parameter_notes: m is the number of outputs of the W-spider (shown for m = 2); holds for any m.
